data: Heavy lift for Artemis lunar program

Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs from the NASA SLS fact sheet (Dec 2025): 322 ft tall, 5.75 million lb fueled, 8.8 million lbf maximum thrust at liftoff; core stage + ICPS with two five-segment solid boosters. Gallery TBD.

NASA’s super-heavy successor to the Space Shuttle stack, sharing its RS-25 engines and SRB heritage. Carried Orion on Artemis I in 2022 and the Artemis II crew around the Moon in 2026; planned to launch crewed missions through Artemis V. The more powerful Block 1B upgrade was cancelled in 2026.
First crewed flight beyond low-Earth orbit since Apollo 17 (1972) — and the mission that inspired this project
First crewed test of the commercial lunar landers — Orion plans to dock with one or both in Earth orbit
First crewed lunar landing since Apollo 17 (1972)
Second crewed landing of the Artemis era — the start of a lunar base
Crew vehicle for the Artemis lunar program
Apollo 10 + Skylab + 53 Shuttle flights; now NASA's SLS / Artemis pad
1970s NASA outer-planet workhorse — Pioneer 10/11, Helios 1/2, Mariner 9/10, Pioneer Venus
Lifted Apollo 7, Skylab crews, and ASTP
Reusable, hydrogen-fuelled, and still flying on SLS
